from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration
        title = "The Summation Machine: A Prerequisite Look"
        lines = [
            "Meet Sigma, our infinite summation robot.",
            "Summing one over n creates a stack growing forever.",
            "This stack is the divergent Harmonic Series.",
            "But some sums settle at a finite height.",
            "These convergent stacks reach a specific limit."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        ROBOT_COLOR = "#00AEFF"
        HARMONIC_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        CONVERGENT_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        LIMIT_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ROBOT_COLOR)
        
        # Using Unicode Sigma symbol in Text instead of Tex LaTeX string
        sigma_symbol = Text("Σ", color=ROBOT_COLOR, font_size=48)
        robot_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=ROBOT_COLOR)
        robot = VGroup(robot_circle, sigma_symbol)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, "B1")
        
        self.play(Create(robot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HARMONIC_COLOR)
        
        base_point = self.grid["F3"] + DOWN * 0.5 # Start slightly below F3
        num_terms = 15
        harmonic_bars = VGroup()
        current_y = base_point[1]
        
        # Scaling height so sum exceeds screen
        scale_h = 2.0
        
        for n in range(1, num_terms + 1):
            h = (1.0 / n) * scale_h
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=1.0, 
                height=h, 
                fill_color=HARMONIC_COLOR, 
                fill_opacity=0.7, 
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to([base_point[0], current_y + h/2, 0])
            harmonic_bars.add(bar)
            current_y += h

        self.play(
            Succession(*[FadeIn(bar, shift=UP*0.1) for bar in harmonic_bars], lag_ratio=0.1),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HARMONIC_COLOR)
        
        label_harmonic = Text("Harmonic Series (Divergent)", font_size=20, color=HARMONIC_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(label_harmonic, "D5")
        
        self.play(Write(label_harmonic))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Transition to convergent series
        self.lecture[3].set_color(CONVERGENT_COLOR)
        
        convergent_bars = VGroup()
        current_y_conv = base_point[1]
        
        for n in range(1, num_terms + 1):
            h = (1.0 / (n**2)) * scale_h
            bar = Rectangle(
                width=1.0, 
                height=h, 
                fill_color=CONVERGENT_COLOR, 
                fill_opacity=0.7, 
                stroke_width=1
            )
            bar.move_to([base_point[0], current_y_conv + h/2, 0])
            convergent_bars.add(bar)
            current_y_conv += h

        label_convergent = Text("Convergent Series", font_size=20, color=CONVERGENT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(label_convergent, "D5")

        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(harmonic_bars, convergent_bars),
            ReplacementTransform(label_harmonic, label_convergent),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(LIMIT_COLOR)
        
        # Limit of 1/n^2 is pi^2/6 approx 1.645. 
        limit_height = 1.64493 * scale_h
        limit_y = base_point[1] + limit_height
        
        dashed_line = DashedLine(
            start=[base_point[0] - 1, limit_y, 0],
            end=[base_point[0] + 3, limit_y, 0],
            color=LIMIT_COLOR
        )
        
        limit_label = Text("Finite Limit", font_size=20, color=LIMIT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(limit_label, "C5") # Positioned relative to the line height
        limit_label.shift(UP * 0.2)

        self.play(
            Create(dashed_line),
            Write(limit_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(Scene):
    """
    Manim CE v0.19.0 script explaining the Riemann Zeta Function.
    Fixes the FileNotFoundError by replacing MathTex (which requires a LaTeX installation)
    with Text using Unicode characters.
    """
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Background and Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        title = Text("The Riemann Zeta Function", font_size=36, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        underline = Underline(title, color=BLUE)
        
        # 2. Lecture Content (Left Side)
        lecture_points = VGroup(
            Text("• Defined for complex numbers s", font_size=24),
            Text("• Infinite sum of integers", font_size=24),
            Text("• Infinite product of primes", font_size=24),
            Text("• The link to Prime Number Theorem", font_size=24)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4).scale(0.8)
        lecture_points.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.8).shift(DOWN * 0.5)

        # 3. Mathematical Formulas (Right Side)
        # Summation Form - Using Text with Unicode to avoid LaTeX dependency
        sum_label = Text("Infinite Series", font_size=20, color=GRAY)
        sum_formula = Text(
            "ζ(s) = ∑ 1/nˢ",
            font_size=42, color=WHITE
        )
        series_group = VGroup(sum_label, sum_formula).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        # Euler Product Form - Using Text with Unicode to avoid LaTeX dependency
        prod_label = Text("Euler Product", font_size=20, color=GRAY)
        prod_formula = Text(
            "ζ(s) = ∏ 1/(1 - p⁻ˢ)",
            font_size=42, color=WHITE
        )
        product_group = VGroup(prod_label, prod_formula).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)

        # Positioning Right Side
        formulas = VGroup(series_group, product_group).arrange(DOWN, buff=1.2)
        formulas.to_edge(RIGHT, buff=1).shift(DOWN * 0.5)

        # 4. Connecting Elements
        arrow = DoubleArrow(
            series_group.get_bottom(), 
            product_group.get_top(), 
            color=YELLOW, 
            stroke_width=3
        )
        bridge_text = Text("The Bridge", font_size=18, color=YELLOW).next_to(arrow, RIGHT)

        # 5. Animation Sequence
        # Title and points
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Create(underline))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        for point in lecture_points:
            self.play(FadeIn(point, shift=RIGHT), run_time=0.7)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # Formulas
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_label), Write(sum_formula))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(
            Create(arrow),
            FadeIn(bridge_text)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(prod_label), Write(prod_formula))
        self.wait(2)

        # Highlighting the connection
        box = SurroundingRectangle(formulas, color=BLUE, buff=0.4)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(3)

        # Final cleanup
        self.play(
            FadeOut(box),
            FadeOut(lecture_points),
            formulas.animate.move_to(ORIGIN).scale(1.2),
            FadeOut(title),
            FadeOut(underline),
            FadeOut(bridge_text),
            FadeOut(arrow)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    """
    Fixed implementation for Section4Scene to resolve FileNotFoundError: 'latex'.
    Uses Text instead of MathTex to avoid dependency on a system LaTeX installation
    while maintaining the visual structure and animation logic.
    """
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.35)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5).shift(UP * 0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define animation grid for the right side (3.5 units right of center)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # x starts at 1.5, moves right; y starts at 2.0, moves down
                x_pos = 1.5 + (j * 0.9)
                y_pos = 2.0 - (i * 0.9)
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x_pos, y_pos, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

    def construct(self):
        # Content Setup
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Euler Product Formula",
            [
                "- Connection to Prime Numbers",
                "- Analytical Bridge to Number Theory",
                "- Fundamental Identity for Re(s) > 1",
                "- Product over all Primes 'p'"
            ]
        )

        # Mathematical Elements
        # Fixed: Changed MathTex to Text to resolve 'latex' executable missing error
        formula = Text(
            "ζ(s) = Σ 1/n^s = Π 1/(1-p^-s)",
            font_size=28,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3")

        # Visual representation of a prime-based object
        prime_structure = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.4, color=BLUE),
            Text("p", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(prime_structure, "D3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        description = Text("Convergence for s > 1", font_size=18, slant=ITALIC)
        self.place_at_grid(description, "E3")

        # Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(self.title), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture, shift=RIGHT), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(formula), run_time=2)
        self.play(Create(prime_structure))
        self.play(FadeIn(description))
        
        # Highlight logic
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color(WHITE).scale(1.1))
        self.play(formula.animate.scale(1/1.1))
        
        self.wait(3)

    def construct(self):
        # 1. Initialize Layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Euler Product Formula", 
            [
                "- The Analytic Bridge",
                "- Identity: Sum = Product",
                "- Mapping Integers to Primes",
                "- Convergence for Re(s) > 1"
            ]
        )

        # 2. Main Formula
        # Replaced MathTex with Text using Unicode to bypass missing LaTeX dependency
        # Zeta(s) = Product over primes p of (1 - p^-s)^-1
        zeta_formula = Text(
            "ζ(s) = Πₚ (1 - p⁻ˢ)⁻¹",
            font_size=36,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        self.place_at_grid(zeta_formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.1)

        self.play(Write(self.title))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture, shift=RIGHT))
        self.play(Write(zeta_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Example Expansion for Primes
        # Replaced MathTex with Text using Unicode to bypass missing LaTeX dependency
        expansion = Text(
            "= (1-2⁻ˢ)⁻¹ · (1-3⁻ˢ)⁻¹ · (1-5⁻ˢ)⁻¹ ...",
            font_size=24,
            color=BLUE_B
        )
        self.place_at_grid(expansion, "D3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(expansion, shift=UP))
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Highlight Connection
        highlight_box = SurroundingRectangle(zeta_formula, color=GOLD, buff=0.2)
        connection_text = Text("Primes", font_size=24, color=GOLD)
        connection_text.next_to(highlight_box, DOWN)

        self.play(Create(highlight_box))
        self.play(Write(connection_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # 5. Final Transition
        self.play(
            FadeOut(zeta_formula),
            FadeOut(expansion),
            FadeOut(highlight_box),
            FadeOut(connection_text)
        )
        
        conclusion = Text("The Foundation of Prime Number Theory", font_size=28, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)
from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup the Coordinate Plane (Complex Plane representation)
        # Fixed: Added label_constructor=Text to avoid the 'latex' dependency
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-10, 5, 2],
            y_range=[-6, 6, 2],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": BLUE_D,
                "stroke_width": 1,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.3
            }
        ).add_coordinates(label_constructor=Text)

        # 2. Riemann Zeta Function Formula
        # Fixed: Changed MathTex to Text with Unicode characters to avoid the 'latex' dependency
        zeta_formula = Text(
            "ζ(s) = Σ 1/nˢ",
            font_size=32
        ).to_corner(UL, buff=0.5).add_background_rectangle()

        # 3. The Critical Line (Re(s) = 1/2)
        critical_line = Line(
            start=plane.coords_to_point(0.5, -4),
            end=plane.coords_to_point(0.5, 4),
            color=YELLOW,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        # Fixed: Changed MathTex to Text to avoid the 'latex' dependency
        critical_label = Text(
            "Re(s) = 1/2", 
            color=YELLOW,
            font_size=24
        ).next_to(critical_line, RIGHT, buff=0.2).shift(UP * 2)

        # 4. Zeroes visualization (Trivial example points)
        zero_points = [
            plane.coords_to_point(0.5, 2),
            plane.coords_to_point(0.5, -2)
        ]
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point, color=RED) for point in zero_points])

        # 5. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Write(zeta_formula))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(critical_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(critical_label, shift=RIGHT))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(dots))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Riemann Zeta Function: The Bridge Between Integers and Primes

sections.title: The Summation Machine: A Prerequisite Look
sections.content: Introduce the concept of infinite series using a 'Summation Robot'. Review the Harmonic Series and convergent geometric series to establish that adding infinite terms can result in a finite number. Visually contrast a series that 'explodes' (diverges) versus one that 'settles' (converges) using a filling water tank analogy.
sections.example: Robot 'Sigma' tries to stack blocks: If the blocks are 1, 1/2, 1/3, the stack grows forever; but if they are 1, 1/4, 1/9, the stack never exceeds a specific height.

sections.title: Defining the Zeta Function ζ(s)
sections.content: Formally introduce the Riemann Zeta Function as the sum of 1/n^s for all integers n from 1 to infinity. Use a slider visual to show how the value of 's' controls how fast the terms shrink. Focus on the real-variable version first to build intuition.
sections.example: A dynamic graph where moving a slider for 's' changes the curve of f(n) = n^-s. When s=2, we see the 'Basel Problem' landscape.

sections.title: The Basel Milestone: When Math Gets Beautiful
sections.content: Present Leonhard Euler’s famous discovery: ζ(2) = π²/6. Use a geometric animation to show how a sum of reciprocal squares unexpectedly relates to the area of a circle. This demonstrates that the Zeta function encodes hidden geometric truths.
sections.example: A circle being 'unrolled' into a line segment whose length is exactly the sum of the infinite square-reciprocal series.

sections.title: Entering the Complex Plane: Analytic Continuation
sections.content: Transition from real numbers to complex numbers (s = σ + it). Explain that the original sum only works for σ > 1, but we can 'stretch' the function to the rest of the map using analytic continuation. Use a visual 'rubber sheet' metaphor where a grid is warped and expanded.
sections.example: An artist stretching a small canvas (the region where s > 1) to cover the entire desk (the complex plane), revealing hidden 'valleys' and 'peaks'.

sections.title: The Euler Product: The Prime Number Connection
sections.content: Introduce the most critical property: The Zeta function can be rewritten as an infinite product involving only Prime Numbers. Explain that this function is the 'DNA' of primes. Show the identity: Σ (1/n^s) = Π (1 / (1 - p^-s)).
sections.example: A 'Prime Sieve' machine where all integers (1, 2, 3...) enter, and the machine extracts a product of primes (2, 3, 5...) that perfectly reconstructs the Zeta function's value.

sections.title: The Million-Dollar Mystery: The Riemann Hypothesis
sections.content: Conclude with the 'zeros' of the function. Explain that where the function equals zero tells us about the distribution of primes. Visualize the 'Critical Line' at Re(s) = 1/2 and show the 'Trivial Zeros' versus the 'Non-trivial Zeros'.
sections.example: A treasure map where all the 'buried treasures' (zeros) are predicted to lie exactly on a single vertical line. If one zero is found off the line, the map of prime numbers breaks.

storyboard.title: Defining the Zeta Function ζ(s)
lecture_lines: The Zeta Function sums reciprocals raised to power s.

storyboard.title: The Basel Milestone: When Math Gets Beautiful
lecture_lines: Euler discovered zeta of two is pi squared over six.
We can unroll a circle to match this sum.
This reveals a bridge between integers and geometry.

storyboard.title: Entering the Complex Plane: Analytic Continuation
lecture_lines: We now extend s into the complex plane.
Analytic continuation stretches the function's reach.
A warped grid reveals the function's hidden landscape.

storyboard.title: The Euler Product: The Prime Number Connection
lecture_lines: We start with the infinite sum over all integers.
We filter every integer through a prime number sieve.
This process isolates primes, our fundamental building blocks.
We transform the sum into an infinite product.
This elegant identity bridges integers and prime numbers.
animations: Display the Zeta summation on the left: \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n^s} in #FFFFFF.
Animate a conveyor belt [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/conveyor.svg] moving integers 2, 3, 4, 5... into a 'Prime Filter' box #FF4500.
Filter out composite numbers, leaving only primes 2, 3, 5, 7,... and highlight them.
Form the Euler product \prod_{p} \frac{1}{1-p^{-s}} on the right side of the screen.
Create a connection line between the sum and the product to show they are identical.

storyboard.title: The Million-Dollar Mystery: The Riemann Hypothesis
lecture_lines: We focus on the critical strip in the complex plane.
Trivial zeros appear at negative even integers.
We draw the critical line at real part one-half.
Riemann hypothesized all non-trivial zeros lie here.
This vertical line remains mathematics' greatest unsolved mystery.
animations: Transition back to the complex plane, focusing on the region between Re(s)=0 and Re(s)=1.
Mark the trivial zeros at s = -2, -4, -6 with white X marks.
Draw a bold red #FF0000 line vertically at Re(s) = 0.5 (the Critical Line).
Animate a sequence of gold dots #FFD700 appearing on this red line, representing the non-trivial zeros.
Zoom out to show the critical line stretching to infinity, with all dots remaining strictly on the line.
